A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAP work and are fully readable, including equations, figures and tables. v1 ends with references; v2 retains the main paper and adds Appendices A–C.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original RAP experiments, including benchmark evaluations, component ablations, retrieval analyses and inference-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendices B–C add search-budget and bias experiments, retriever comparisons, expanded baseline results and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The core RAP, Spatial-Awareness Layout and RE-Search procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 introduces a SigLIP retrieval variant that uses an MLLM to extract noun phrases before retrieval, a limited procedural adaptation. Appendix A otherwise supplies implementation documentation rather than establishing a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds DocVQA document-retrieval evaluation alongside the retained perception benchmarks. V*Bench, HR-Bench 4K/8K and MME-RealWorld coverage remains unchanged; the new sensitivity tests and qualitative cases stay within existing perception tasks.

E2.justification: v1 directly compared DC2 and Zoom Eye with RAP only using LLaVA-v1.5-13B on HR-Bench 4K in Table 5. Table 8 substantially expands their participation across 7B/13B models and the existing V*Bench and HR-Bench evaluations. Table 7 also introduces the SigLIP–VisRAG retriever comparison.

E3.justification: New targeted protocols include fixed search budgets spanning 1–200 steps with early stopping disabled by setting tau to infinity, a bias sweep from 0 to 1, and DocVQA evaluation using MRR@10. These supplement the retained main experiments; Appendix A's newly specified defaults do not establish changes to their original settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's layout, crop-count and component analyses, Appendices B.1–B.3 add search-budget scaling, bias sensitivity and retriever substitution experiments. Appendix C adds comparative cases examining crop-boundary information loss, incorrect search paths and insufficient spatial context.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added sensitivity plots continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 are unchanged, but Tables 7–8 and Figures 5–8 add substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. Table 7 reports HR-Bench 8K averages of 51.9 with SigLIP and 63.5 with VisRAG. Table 8 newly reports 13B Zoom Eye scores of 56.4 overall and 45.5 FCP, versus retained RAP scores of 59.3 and 42.0. Repeated RAP rows are not improved scores between versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the spatial mapping definitions and the heuristic-cost formulation are unchanged. Algorithm 2 restates existing mathematics in pseudocode; no new theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion are unchanged. The novelty claim, training-free framework, spatial-layout contribution, adaptive retrieval claim and headline performance claims retain their original scope.

C2.justification: The appendix adds interpretations linking search-scaling benefits to model capability and spatial combinations, discusses sensitivity to bias and retrieval quality, and attributes particular baseline failures to missing visual context. These extend the existing mechanism discussion without revising its central explanation or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents padding, exclusion of zero-valued crops, retention ratios of 25%, 50% and 75%, a 200-step search limit, and full search pseudocode. Appendix B.3 supplies retriever sizes and noun-phrase preprocessing. These materially expand implementation information; the existing bias, confidence threshold and code-availability statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SigLIP reference, Zhai et al. (2023), and expands discussion of comparisons with already-cited DC2 and Zoom Eye. Section 2 and the central positioning of RAP relative to prior research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an appendix roadmap and organized implementation, experimental and case-study sections. The existing main text is not rewritten or reordered; its only textual change is the version stamp.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 2, two multipanel experimental plots, two qualitative comparison figures and Tables 7–8. This substantially expands the visual presentation. Some table rows and the waterfall example reuse existing material, while all original figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added sensitivity tests, fuller matched baseline comparisons and disclosed search defaults improve empirical assessment and implementation transparency. However, new Algorithm 2 evaluates 1/d at depth zero and updates the best node toward higher cost despite minimizing node selection. Appendix B.4 also presents FSP scores 73.8/72.3 without distinguishing them from overall scores 57.1/53.8. These reproducibility and reporting inconsistencies limit the net improvement.
